raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Resolve Gemma4's audio extractor consistently with input validation: prefer `feature_extractor`, then fall back to `audio_processor`. Both `_get_mm_inputs` and the audio token expansion path must use the same resolved component and sampling rate.

The earlier guard that could suggest silently emitting a single token when an extractor is absent has been removed. If neither component exists, the existing `_validate_input` raises `ValueError: Audio feature extractor was not found...` before preprocessing. Single-token output remains intentional only when `expand_mm_tokens=False`.

Normally merged current main `9997aa07`, resolving the test conflict while retaining main's XPU coverage marker. The net contribution is two files; no model definitions, dependencies or training behavior are changed.

## Regression coverage

The existing lightweight test now has ten cases:

- Feature extractor only; audio processor with the feature attribute missing; audio processor with the feature attribute explicitly None; both components present, preferring the feature extractor.
- Enabled/disabled token expansion, selected sampling rate, extractor invocation and unchanged input messages.
- Both components absent or None must raise the existing clear validation error.

These execute the real `process_messages` and `_get_mm_inputs`. Only audio-I/O normalization and the external processor are controlled; no replacement implementation of the plugin is tested.

On unchanged main `9997aa07`, with the production module path verified: **2 failed, 8 passed** (the two enabled-expansion fallback cases fail by calling None). With this PR: **10 passed**, then independently repeated twice after the final edit.

## Validation and limits

- Changed-file Ruff 0.15.5 lint and formatting checks, plus `git diff --check`, pass.
- Full `make quality` is not green: current main has a W293 finding in unchanged `model/patcher.py`; the independent full formatting check lists four untouched baseline files. These were not folded into this fix.
- The broader existing base-plugin test cannot load an uncached tiny tokenizer in enforced offline mode. No model/tokenizer was downloaded, and the model-dependent suite, GPU training and native Windows integration were not run.
- macOS / Python 3.13, cached Torch 2.14.1, torchaudio 2.11.0, Transformers 5.8.0. `DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1` was used with this existing local environment; this is not a claim of an exact locked dependency-matrix run.

AI-assisted investigation, conflict resolution, self-review and repeated testing. Maintainer review is still requested; local validation is not merge approval or hosted CI success.

Preserved the fix and tightened the comment to explain WHY (text-only checkpoints / partial offline loads can land here without `feature_extractor`).

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a safety check when accessing the feature extractor in src/llamafactory/data/mm_plugin.py to prevent potential errors during audio token computation. The reviewer suggested optimizing performance by moving the attribute lookup outside the nested loops and adding a fallback for audio_processor to ensure consistency with other parts of the codebase.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `getattr` call is placed inside a nested loop (`for message in messages` -> `while AUDIO_PLACEHOLDER in content`), which is inefficient as the `processor` object and its attributes do not change during this process. Consider moving this assignment before the `for message in messages:` loop (around line 743) to avoid redundant lookups.

Additionally, to be consistent with the validation logic in `_validate_input` (lines 158-160), it should also check for `audio_processor` if `feature_extractor` is missing or `None`.

```suggestion
                feature_extractor = getattr(processor, "feature_extractor", None) or getattr(processor, "audio_processor", None)
```

nodes.body:
The `or audio_processor` fallback looks right, but the second half of the change trades a loud failure for a quiet one. When `feature_extractor` is None and `expand_mm_tokens` is True, this now takes the `else` branch and emits a single un-expanded audio placeholder, so the prompt carries the wrong number of audio tokens and the run fails later inside the model with a shape error that points nowhere near here.

If a processor really can arrive without any audio extractor while audio inputs are present, raising with a message that names the missing component would be more useful than silently under-expanding.

+        )
 
         if self.expand_mm_tokens:
             mm_inputs = self._get_mm_inputs(images, videos, audios, processor)
@@ -1132,9 +1137,10 @@ def process_messages(
 
             while AUDIO_PLACEHOLDER in content:
                 current_audio = next(audio_iter)
+                # Input validation rejects a missing audio extractor before expansion.
                 if self.expand_mm_tokens:
                     num_audio_tokens = processor._compute_audio_num_tokens(
-                        current_audio, processor.feature_extractor.sampling_rate
+                        current_audio, feature_extractor.sampling_rate
                     )
                     audio_str = f"{boa_token}{audio_token * num_audio_tokens}{eoa_token}"
                 else:

@@ -244,6 +244,77 @@ def test_gemma4_plugin():
     _check_plugin(**check_inputs)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("extractor_source", ["feature", "audio_missing_feature", "audio_none_feature", "both"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("expand_mm_tokens", [True, False])
+def test_gemma4_plugin_uses_audio_processor_fallback(monkeypatch, extractor_source, expand_mm_tokens):
+    extractor_calls, sampling_rates = [], []
+
+    class AudioProcessor:
+        def __init__(self, name, sampling_rate):
+            self.name = name
+            self.sampling_rate = sampling_rate
+
+        def __call__(self, audios, **kwargs):
+            extractor_calls.append(self.name)
+            return {}
+
+    class Processor:
+        image_token = "<|image|>"
+        video_token = "<|video|>"
+        audio_token = "<|audio|>"
+        boi_token = "<start_of_image>"
+        eoi_token = "<end_of_image>"
+        boa_token = "<start_of_audio>"
+        eoa_token = "<end_of_audio>"
+        audio_processor = AudioProcessor("audio", 16000)
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def _compute_audio_num_tokens(audio, sampling_rate):
+            sampling_rates.append(sampling_rate)
+            return 2
+
+    if extractor_source in {"feature", "both"}:
+        Processor.feature_extractor = AudioProcessor("feature", 22050)
+    elif extractor_source == "audio_none_feature":
+        Processor.feature_extractor = None
+
+    if extractor_source == "feature":
+        Processor.audio_processor = None
+
+    gemma4_plugin = get_mm_plugin(name="gemma4", audio_token="<|audio|>")
+    gemma4_plugin.expand_mm_tokens = expand_mm_tokens
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gemma4_plugin,
+        "_regularize_audios",
+        lambda audios, **kwargs: {"audios": audios},
+    )
+    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "<audio>"}]
+
+    processed = gemma4_plugin.process_messages(messages, NO_IMAGES, NO_VIDEOS, AUDIOS, Processor())
+
+    expected_audio_tokens = "<|audio|>" * (2 if expand_mm_tokens else 1)
+    assert processed == [
+        {
+            "role": "user",
+            "content": f"<start_of_audio>{expected_audio_tokens}<end_of_audio>",
+        }
+    ]
+    expected_source = "feature" if extractor_source in {"feature", "both"} else "audio"
+    assert extractor_calls == ([expected_source] if expand_mm_tokens else [])
+    assert sampling_rates == ([22050 if expected_source == "feature" else 16000] if expand_mm_tokens else [])
+    assert messages == [{"role": "user", "content": "<audio>"}]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("extractors", [{}, {"feature_extractor": None, "audio_processor": None}])
+def test_gemma4_plugin_rejects_missing_audio_extractor(extractors):
+    plugin = get_mm_plugin(name="gemma4", audio_token="<|audio|>")
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Audio feature extractor was not found"):
+        plugin.process_messages(
+            [{"role": "user", "content": "<audio>"}], NO_IMAGES, NO_VIDEOS, AUDIOS, SimpleNamespace(**extractors)
+        )
+
+
 @pytest.mark.runs_on(["cpu", "mps", "xpu"])
 @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_transformers_version_greater_than("4.52.0"), reason="Requires transformers>=4.52.0")
 def test_internvl_plugin():
